questions.q: What is the core trade-off between managed Kafka and self-hosted Kafka, per this lesson?
options: They trade different costs for different control — neither is simply better in all cases
Managed Kafka is always more expensive in every scenario
Self-hosted Kafka has no operational responsibilities at all
There is no real difference between the two options
questions.explain: The lesson frames this explicitly as a trade-off, not a one-size-fits-all answer.

questions.q: Which of these is listed as a concrete part of the 'ops burden' a managed service takes off a team's plate?
options: Capacity planning, patching brokers, and handling failure recovery
Writing the Kafka producer application's business logic
Choosing which programming language to use
Designing the company's marketing website
questions.explain: These are the concrete operational responsibilities described — sizing, patching, and recovering from broker failures.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when can self-hosting end up cheaper than a managed service?
options: At very large, sustained throughput, when the team already has in-house Kafka expertise on staff for other reasons
Only when the team has never run Kafka before
Self-hosting is never cheaper under any circumstances
Only when throughput is small and unpredictable
questions.explain: Managed pricing bakes in a margin for the ops work being done for you; at large scale with existing expertise, that margin can outweigh doing it in-house.

questions.q: How do managed Kafka services like Confluent Cloud and Event Hubs typically price their offering, per this lesson?
options: Based on throughput and storage, instead of by server or broker count
A flat one-time fee regardless of usage
Based purely on the number of employees at the customer's company
They are always free with no cost model
questions.explain: This is the direct trade against paying an engineer's time to do the ops-burden list themselves.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend for teams that don't fit cleanly into either 'always managed' or 'always self-hosted'?
options: Many real teams use both — self-hosted for a core high-throughput system, managed for smaller or newer workloads
A team must pick exactly one option and can never mix approaches
Managed and self-hosted Kafka cannot coexist in the same organization
Self-hosting is required before any managed service can be used
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly describes a hybrid approach as common in practice.
